🌐 Worldline Engine

Run one worldline. Compare many. Explore the space of possible worlds.

A deterministic, domain-neutral execution kernel for multi-agent worlds. It places goal-driven entities inside a discrete timeline and gives every step a stable answer: what happened, when it happened, what was committed, what failed — then lets you replay it, branch it, and compare it against a thousand other futures.

--- ## ✨ Why Worldline Engine? Most agent frameworks are one-shot demos: run once, get lucky, throw it away. Worldline is built on a different conviction — **the value of a world is not a single "correct" future, it is the space of possibilities**. Small perturbations, amplified by the system, produce macroscopically different outcomes. That is the butterfly effect, and it is exactly what we want to observe. - 🌌 **Worldlines, not worlds** — a worldline is the pair **(manifest, recorded stream)**: the manifest pins everything that defines the run (engine version, world code, population hash, model, prompts, policies); the `seed` is only the random-stream parameter. Deterministic scheduling keeps a single worldline internally consistent, auditable, and replayable. Two worldlines are comparable exactly when their manifests differ in one field. - 🔁 **Byte-level replay** — same manifest, same inputs, same LLM response stream → identical world. Checkpoints, resume, and appended events mean long experiments never restart from zero. - 🧪 **Isolated failure** — tentative actions are staged and validated before they touch world state. A bad agent cannot pollute the world. - ⏱️ **Time with structure** — ticks and turns make long-running interactions observable, not a black box. - 🧩 **Domain-neutral by design** — the engine does not tell you what to simulate. A city, a market, a game, or a crowd of people: your `World` owns the meaning; the engine owns execution. - 🪶 **Zero required dependencies** — pure Python 3.11+ standard library. No LLM SDK, no vector database, no framework lock-in. > 🦋 **The butterfly is a feature — and a measurement.** We do not try to predict > *the* future. We rehearse many, so that decisions can be made against the whole > distribution of what could happen. Divergence across worldlines is the > measurement, not the conclusion: the object of study is the shape of the > distribution — what stays stable across seeds, where worlds part ways, which > outcomes attract. ## 🏗️ Architecture ```mermaid graph TD subgraph "One deterministic tick" S["Scheduler
(All / Random activation)"] --> T["Turns"] T --> C["Controller
(Rule · Replay · LLM)"] C -->|"ActionIntent"| W["World
(domain rules & state)"] W -->|"validated"| R["resolve_and_apply
(atomic commit)"] end subgraph "Persistence & replay" R -->|"checkpoint"| DB[("StateStore
SQLite / in-memory")] R -->|"events"| EV[("EventSink
SQLite / JSONL / memory")] DB -.->|"restore_latest"| S end ``` The engine protocol is small and stable: `Simulation`, `World`, `Controller`, `Scheduler`, `StateStore`, `EventSink`. Your `World` implements snapshot, observe, validate and commit; your `Controller` proposes `ActionIntent`s; everything else is the engine's job. ## 🚀 Quick Start ```powershell python -m pip install -e . python -m unittest discover -s tests -v ``` Run the minimal closed loop from [examples/counter_simulation.py](examples/counter_simulation.py): two entities act on the same worldline, results are saved, and you can resume, replay, or branch from any checkpoint. ## 📦 Core Concepts | Concept | Responsibility | |---|---| | `Simulation` | Owns the timeline: ticks, turns, budgets, failure semantics | | `World` | Sole owner of domain rules and domain state | | `Controller` | Proposes `ActionIntent`s (rule, replay, or LLM) — never mutates state | | `Scheduler` | Decides who acts in each tick (deterministic) | | `StateStore` / `EventSink` | Checkpoints, events and replay trail | ### Worldline identity Pass `manifest={...}` to `Simulation` and the runtime records it as a `worldline_manifest` event — the very first event of the run, emitted before `simulation_started` and never re-emitted when a run is restored from a checkpoint. The engine treats the manifest as opaque data: your `World` and upper layers decide what pins a worldline (population hashes, model ids, prompt hashes, policies). The seed is only the random-stream parameter — two runs with the same seed but different manifests are different worldlines, and an intervention experiment is a pair of runs whose manifests differ in exactly one field. ## 🗺️ Roadmap - [ ] Batch worldline exploration: stability across seeds at each tick, divergence curves over time, attractor clustering of final states - [ ] Null-baseline tooling for intervention experiments (same manifest, different seeds as the control) - [ ] Distributed execution for very large worlds - [ ] Stable v1.0 execution semantics ## 🤝 Contributing PRs are welcome! Please follow [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/). Bugs, ideas and experiments → [Issues](https://github.com/Lecheeel/worldline-engine/issues). Built for the social domain? See [Worldline Social](https://github.com/Lecheeel/worldline-social), a reproducible social simulation built on this engine. ## 📄 License Apache License 2.0. See [LICENSE](LICENSE).
